I carried a knife on my left hip and drove a tractor to plow the fields even though I could barely reach the peddles. I got up at 3am, dressed myself and went with the rest of the men to bottle feed the calves. I caught the bus at 6a with the rest of my 4 siblings; I was the oldest.

We had great teachers that commanded respect, taught us history, made us memorize the 23 Psalm, the Bill of Rights and the Gettysburg Address. We pledged allegiance to the Flag and ask God to forgive us so we could become better in His sight. Our lunches at school were free and homemade, you could eat all you wanted and I did.

Our mothers stayed home and participated with our homework. We stood against the living room wall as she did a pretend spelling bee with us kids and then made us homemade supper. Our father was one of little words whose clothes were always soaked in sweat, his hand dark and callous. We were disciplined with a switch, cane or an open hand. We all knew at one point in time we all would suffer losses. We learn the realities of life early.

It was a rewarding life to grow all your vegetables, make honey, milk cows for milk, butter and cream and slaughtered them in the fall. Had chickens for eggs and sugar cane. We burned wood for heat and didn't have air conditioning. We were required to read one book per week and relay what we read.
